alternates.fact: Tree-climbing is not typical lion behavior across Africa; the only other population known for it with any regularity lives in Uganda's Ishasha sector of Queen Elizabeth National Park.
alternates.why: I've literally seen lions in a tree in Tanzania and never questioned it, so finding out it's basically only us and one spot in Uganda is a proper 'no way' for the group chat.

alternates.claim: The tree-climbing lions in Tanzania are the only lions in the world that climb trees.

alternates.aside: Corrected. You pasted: "The tree-climbing lions in Tanzania are the only lions in the world that climb trees". The document says the tree-climbing lions of Lake Manyara are not the only ones in the world: another population in Uganda's Ishasha sector climbs trees with some regularity.
